Regular expressions for sample identifiers

regex_ids.Rd

regex_ids is a centralised place for regular expressions (regex) for extracting different identifiers. These expressions are then used by the extract_* series of functions for extracting identifiers.

Regular expressions are written as raw strings using stringr::regex which makes them easier to understand and maintain. The "Regular Expressions" chapter in "R for Data Science" is a great resource for understanding regular expressions.

Usage

regex_ids()

Value

A named list of regular expressions for different identifiers

DNA Database identifiers

worksheet: the worksheet identifier is "WS" followed by six numbers, which increase sequentially (i.e "WS000001", "WS000002", WS000003"). Worksheets are the way in which genetic tests are organised into batches within the lab. Worksheet identifiers are generated by DNA Database.

combined_plate: the combined plate number from the DNA Database which is "CP" followed by 5 digits. "Combined plates" are created by combining muliple worksheets together.

labno: the numeric identifier given to every DNA sample from DNA Database. This identifier is referred to as "labno" throughout idtools because this is the name used in the "Samples" table of DNA Database.

The regex specifies 8 digits in the identifier. Note: samples from 2012 and earlier have only 6 digits in the identifier, and these will not be extracted by idtools.

The first two digits of the labno format are the year the sample was received, and then the digits increase with each new sample. For example, the first sample received in 2026 would have the labno 26000001.

suffix: if the same DNA sample is tested multiple times on the same worksheet (which can happen for repeatability experiments during test validation) then a suffix letter (usually a-d) is added directly after the labno. Extracting this suffix is useful when assessing the variability between different replicates of the same sample.

iGene identifiers

iGene identifiers have a consistent format of a letter signifying the identifier type (R, S, D or T), followed by a consistent core identifier format.

igene_core: the core iGene regex consists of the two-digit year number, a hyphen, and then four alpha-numeric characters. Example: R26-AB12.

igene_rno: the R (referral) number. One referral may have more than one sample associated with it.

igene_sno: the S (sample) number. One sample may have more than one DNA extraction derived from it.

igene_dno: the D (derivative) number signifies the extraction-specific identifier for a sample. One derivative may have more than one test associated with it.

igene_tno: a T (test) number is given to a specific instance of a test performed on a derivate sample.

Whole genome sequencing identifiers

wgs_patient_no: the whole genome sequencing (WGS) pathway in the Genomic Medicine Service uses a patient identifier which is "p" followed by 11 digits.

wgs_referral_no: the referral ("r") equivalent of the WGS patient number, structured as "r" followed by 11 digits.

Examples


file_string <- "WS123456_12345678_sequencing_results.xlsx"

stringr::str_extract(file_string,
                      pattern = regex_ids()$labno_suffix$regex,
                      group = regex_ids()$labno_suffix$labno_group)
#> [1] "12345678"
